A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adaptive Delay Model (ADM) study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including v4's additional Appendices G–I.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic recovery and timing experiments, two-region and five-region neural-recording analyses, and GP-regression results in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v4 reports these empirical studies and additional synthetic sensitivity, baseline-comparison and visual-stimulus decoding results in Appendices G–H.

M1.justification: Equation 11 changes the augmented process-noise covariance's lower block from I to sigma I, with sigma described as a small stability constant. This revises the stated model locally; the latent decomposition, kernels, time-varying delays and parallel Kalman-EM procedure remain.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds three-class visual-orientation decoding for 0, 90 and 135 degrees using the retained five-region neural dataset. The original neural-recording datasets and GP-regression task remain. Synthetic region-count and dimension sweeps extend settings within the existing simulation task.

E2.justification: Figure 9 adds DLAG, MRM-GP and mp-srSLDS comparisons on the Section 4.1 synthetic dataset, which lacked these comparisons in v2. mp-srSLDS was previously discussed but not evaluated. Existing neural-data and GP-regression comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The selected five-region model order changes from P=2 to P=5. Appendix G adds evaluations across 2–5 regions, 4–10 latents, 200–800 time points and latent-count misspecification, using delay MSE and Pearson correlation. Appendix H introduces linear decoding with three input representations and classification accuracy. These substantially expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's order-P sensitivity checks, Appendix G tests delay recovery against region count, latent dimension and sequence length, plus under- and over-specification of latent counts. Appendix H probes stimulus information in raw observations versus across-region and within-region representations, adding substantial robustness and representation analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over five random seeds, identify Figure 1's shading as across-run variance, and include uncertainty values in Tables 1–2. Additional v4 plots extend uncertainty displays to new results without reporting a changed run-count policy or new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 2 revises neural delays, latent trajectories and likelihood values, sharply narrowing ADM's reported advantage over MRM-GP and DLAG. Figure 3 also revises results; its changed P precludes a direct same-setting performance comparison. Runtime axes change from seconds to minutes. Appendices G–H add findings, while v2 Figure 6(B)'s additional delay results disappear. Tables 1–2 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B revises the EM derivation to use time-dependent transition and noise matrices, a summed log-determinant term, outer-product moment definitions and revised lag indices. Equation 11 also changes the augmented covariance definition. These are local mathematical revisions; the principal GP-to-SSM derivation in Appendix A remains.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central contributions: connecting stationary GPs with SSMs, learning continuously varying multi-region delays without discrete switching states, and parallel inference with logarithmic temporal complexity. Additional experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the interpretation of eventual forward dominance with sustained, accelerating feedback in one communication group and an early direction reversal in the other. Section 2.3 adds a smoothing explanation for the shared length scale. Appendices G–H introduce interpretations concerning amplitude error, preserved delay patterns and information loss through dimensionality reduction.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-availability link, explicitly states matched latent counts for the V1–V2 comparison and mDLAG's three communication channels, and explains sigma's numerical-stability role. These improve documentation; the newly stated comparator settings do not establish that previously different settings were used.

R1.justification: v4 adds Wang et al. (2023, 2024) in the introduction and an Appendix I discussing neural alignment and task-dependent variability through Williams et al., Safaie et al. and Balzani et al.'s TAME-GP. Existing positioning against GP and delay models remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the existing section sequence are retained. Changes include localized rewrites of Section 4.2 and Appendix B, expanded explanations, an acknowledgement and impact statement, and additional appendix sections. This is not a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Main figures receive revised scales, labels, arrows and panel arrangements; appendix latent plots are merged and reconfigured, and new Figures 7–10 are added. The factor-analysis plot is retained as renumbered Figure 6, and Tables 1–2 are reformatted.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the added sensitivity and misspecification tests provide more direct evidence about robustness, while stimulus decoding tests the learned subspaces' functional relevance. Code-access information also improves reproducibility. The gains are limited by sparse documentation of new protocols, removal of additional five-region delay plots, and Section 5's insufficiently updated summary of the revised V1–V2 findings.
